"""Validation of the shape-C robot + the real controller code (core/controller.cpp) in MuJoCo. python3 run_tests.py -> prints the report, writes results/report.json and plots Every run uses domain randomisation unless stated: mass ±8 %, CoM ±4 mm (x) / -6..+8 mm (z), inertia -15/+20 %, tyre friction 0.5-1.2, battery 21-25 V, motor torque ±10 %, 2-4 ms actuation delay, IMU bias + 1.5° mount tilt. """ import json, math, pathlib, sys, numpy as np from multiprocessing import Pool from botsim import BotSim, STATES, CTRL_DT OUT = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent / "results"; OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True) DEG = math.degrees def arr(s): return np.array(s.log) def standup_trial(args): seed, side = args s = BotSim(seed=seed, randomize=True) s.place(pitch=1.8 * side) detected = None for _ in range(int(5.0 / CTRL_DT)): o = s.step() if detected is None and o.state == 2: detected = o.side # side it decided on when it started the lift L = arr(s); s.close() st = L[:, 1].astype(int) up = np.where(st == 4)[0] ok = st[-1] == 4 and np.abs(L[-500:, 2]).max() < math.radians(12) lift = np.where(st == 2)[0] t_up = (L[up[0], 0] - L[lift[0], 0]) if len(up) and len(lift) else float("nan") tries = int(np.sum(np.diff((st == 2).astype(int)) == 1)) return dict(seed=seed, side=side, detected=int(detected or 0), ok=bool(ok), t_up=t_up, tries=tries, vmax=float(np.abs(L[:, 5]).max()), travel=float(np.hypot(L[-1, 9] - L[0, 9], L[-1, 10] - L[0, 10]))) def balance_trial(seed): s = BotSim(seed=seed, randomize=True) s.place(0.0); s.hold() s.run(10.0) L = arr(s) drift = float(np.hypot(L[-1, 9], L[-1, 10])) pitch_rms = float(np.degrees(np.std(L[2500:, 2]))) # push: 10 N for 0.1 s on the body (1 N·s, a firm shove), forwards then backwards res = [] for f in (10.0, -10.0): for _ in range(50): s.step(push=np.array([f, 0, 0])) s.run(4.0) L = arr(s) fell = bool((L[-2050:, 1] != 4).any()) res.append(dict(ok=bool(L[-1, 1] == 4) and not fell, max_pitch=float(DEG(np.abs(L[-2050:, 2]).max())), displaced=float(np.abs(L[-2050:, 9] - L[-2051, 9]).max()))) s.close() return dict(seed=seed, drift_10s=drift, pitch_rms=pitch_rms, pushes=res) def mission(seed=None, video=False): """Back-down start -> stand up -> stand still -> accelerate/cruise/stop -> turns -> arc -> stand still.""" s = BotSim(seed=seed or 0, randomize=seed is not None) s.place(pitch=-1.8) marks = [] def phase(name, secs, **cmd): t0 = s.t; s.run(secs, **cmd); marks.append((name, t0, s.t)) phase("stand up (lying on its back)", 4.0) phase("stand still", 3.0, mode=0, v=0.0, yaw_rate=0.0) phase("accelerate to 1.0 m/s and cruise", 3.0, v=1.0) phase("stop", 3.0, v=0.0) phase("turn +90°", 3.0, mode=2, angle=math.radians(90), seq=1) phase("turn +180°", 4.0, mode=2, angle=math.radians(180), seq=2) phase("turn -135°", 3.5, mode=2, angle=math.radians(-135), seq=3) phase("turn to heading 30°", 3.5, mode=1, angle=math.radians(30)) phase("reverse 0.4 m/s", 3.0, mode=0, v=-0.4, yaw_rate=0.0) phase("arc: 0.5 m/s, 1 rad/s", 3.0, mode=0, v=0.5, yaw_rate=1.0) phase("stop and stand still", 4.0, mode=0, v=0.0, yaw_rate=0.0) L = arr(s) t = L[:, 0] def sl(name): for n, a, b in marks: if n == name: return (t > a) & (t <= b) yaw0 = L[sl("stand still"), 11][-1] rep = {} m = sl("stand still") rep["stand still: drift (mm)"] = 1000 * float(np.hypot(*(L[m][-1, 9:11] - L[m][0, 9:11]))) rep["stand still: pitch wobble (deg, std)"] = float(DEG(np.std(L[m, 2]))) m = sl("accelerate to 1.0 m/s and cruise") vt = np.gradient(L[:, 9], t) * np.cos(L[:, 11]) + np.gradient(L[:, 10], t) * np.sin(L[:, 11]) rep["cruise: true speed over last 1 s (m/s)"] = float(np.mean(vt[m][-500:])) rep["cruise: max pitch (deg)"] = float(DEG(np.abs(L[m, 2]).max())) m = sl("stop") x_stop_cmd = L[m][0, 9:11] rep["stop: distance after the stop command (m)"] = float(np.hypot(*(L[m][-1, 9:11] - x_stop_cmd))) rep["stop: residual speed after 3 s (m/s)"] = float(abs(vt[m][-1])) targets = [("turn +90°", 90), ("turn +180°", 270), ("turn -135°", 135), ("turn to heading 30°", None)] for name, rel in targets: m = sl(name) yaw_end = L[m][-1, 11] if rel is None: # absolute heading 30° in the robot's own heading frame (yaw estimate = 0 at power-up) m0 = sl("stand still"); offset = L[m0][-1, 11] - L[m0][-1, 4] # true - estimated heading err = DEG(math.remainder(yaw_end - (offset + math.radians(30)), 2 * math.pi)) else: err = DEG(math.remainder(yaw_end - (yaw0 + math.radians(rel)), 2 * math.pi)) rep[f"{name}: heading error (deg)"] = float(err) rep[f"{name}: position drift while turning (mm)"] = 1000 * float(np.hypot(*(L[m][-1, 9:11] - L[m][0, 9:11]))) m = sl("stop and stand still") rep["final: still balancing"] = bool(L[-1, 1] == 4) rep["final: drift in the last 2 s (mm)"] = 1000 * float(np.hypot(*(L[-1, 9:11] - L[-1000, 9:11]))) rep["whole mission: max |pitch| after stand-up (deg)"] = float(DEG(np.abs(L[t > 4.0, 2]).max())) rep["odometry error at the end (mm)"] = 1000 * float(np.hypot(L[-1, 12] - (L[-1, 9] - L[0, 9]), L[-1, 13] - (L[-1, 10] - L[0, 10]))) s.close() return rep, marks, L def fall_recovery(seed=7): s = BotSim(seed=seed, randomize=True) s.place(0.0); s.hold(); s.run(1.0) for _ in range(50): s.step(push=np.array([40.0, 0, 0])) # big shove (2 N·s): it falls over s.run(5.0) L = arr(s); st = L[:, 1].astype(int) seq = [STATES[st[i]] for i in range(len(st)) if i == 0 or st[i] != st[i - 1]] s.close() return dict(states=seq, back_up=bool(st[-1] == 4)) if __name__ == "__main__": N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 30 with Pool(2) as pool: su = pool.map(standup_trial, [(3000 + i, side) for i in range(N) for side in (1, -1)]) bal = pool.map(balance_trial, range(4000, 4000 + max(6, N // 3))) report = {} for side, name in ((1, "face-down"), (-1, "back-down")): r = [x for x in su if x["side"] == side] report[f"stand-up from {name}"] = dict( success=f"{sum(x['ok'] for x in r)}/{len(r)}", side_detected_correctly=f"{sum(x['detected'] == side for x in r)}/{len(r)}", first_try=f"{sum(x['ok'] and x['tries'] == 1 for x in r)}/{len(r)}", median_time_s=round(float(np.nanmedian([x['t_up'] for x in r])), 3), max_time_s=round(float(np.nanmax([x['t_up'] for x in r])), 3), peak_speed_m_s=round(float(np.median([x['vmax'] for x in r])), 2), median_travel_m=round(float(np.median([x['travel'] for x in r])), 2), max_travel_m=round(float(np.max([x['travel'] for x in r])), 2)) report["balance 10 s (randomised)"] = dict( runs=len(bal), median_drift_mm=round(1000 * float(np.median([b['drift_10s'] for b in bal])), 1), max_drift_mm=round(1000 * float(np.max([b['drift_10s'] for b in bal])), 1), pitch_std_deg=round(float(np.median([b['pitch_rms'] for b in bal])), 3), push_recovered=f"{sum(p['ok'] for b in bal for p in b['pushes'])}/{2 * len(bal)}", push_max_pitch_deg=round(float(max(p['max_pitch'] for b in bal for p in b['pushes'])), 1)) rep, marks, L = mission(None) report["mission (nominal robot)"] = {k: (round(v, 3) if isinstance(v, float) else v) for k, v in rep.items()} rep2, _, _ = mission(seed=4242) report["mission (randomised robot)"] = {k: (round(v, 3) if isinstance(v, float) else v) for k, v in rep2.items()} report["knocked over -> gets up again"] = fall_recovery() json.dump(report, open(OUT / "report.json", "w"), indent=1) np.save(OUT / "mission_log.npy", L); json.dump(marks, open(OUT / "mission_marks.json", "w")) print(json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False))

import numpy as np, sys, itertools from multiprocessing import Pool from botsim import BotSim, LIB def stand(a): seed,side,ra,hold=a; s=BotSim(seed=seed,randomize=True); LIB.bot_recover(s.ctl,ra,hold); s.place(1.8*side); s.run(2.5) L=np.array(s.log); st=L[:,1].astype(int) first=(np.diff((st==2).astype(int))==1).sum()==1 return bool(L[-1,1]==4 and first) if __name__=="__main__": N=20 with Pool(2) as p: for ra,hold in itertools.product([0.5,1.0,3.0,6.0],[0.0,0.3]): u=p.map(stand,[(7000+i,sd,ra,hold) for i in range(N) for sd in (1,-1)]) print(ra,hold,f"first-try stand-up: {sum(u)}/{2*N}",flush=True)

"""Sweep stand-up parameters over randomised robots, both lying sides (runs in parallel).""" import sys, numpy as np, itertools, math from multiprocessing import Pool from botsim import BotSim, STATES, LIB def trial(args): seed, side, lift, epush, eg, catch, et = args s = BotSim(seed=seed, randomize=True) LIB.bot_tune(s.ctl, lift, 0.6, epush, catch); LIB.bot_lift_mode(s.ctl, 0, eg, et) s.place(pitch=1.8 * side) s.run(5.0) L = np.array(s.log); s.close() st = L[:, 1].astype(int) ok = st[-1] == 4 and np.abs(L[-500:, 2]).max() < math.radians(12) up = np.where(st == 4)[0] return ok, (L[up[0], 0] - 0.3 if len(up) else np.nan), np.abs(L[:, 5]).max(), np.hypot(L[-1, 9], L[-1, 10]) if __name__ == "__main__": N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 6 grid = list(itertools.product([float(v) for v in (sys.argv[2].split(",") if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ["1.6"])], [30], [0.03], [0.35, 0.5], [0, 4, 8])) with Pool(8) as pool: for lift, epush, eg, catch, et in grid: res = pool.map(trial, [(2000 + i, side, lift, epush, eg, catch, et) for i in range(N) for side in (1, -1)]) ok = sum(r[0] for r in res) print(f"lift {lift} epush {epush} eg {eg} catch {catch} et {et}: {ok}/{len(res)} t_up {np.nanmedian([r[1] for r in res]):.2f}s " f"vmax {np.median([r[2] for r in res]):.2f} travel {np.median([r[3] for r in res]):.2f} m", flush=True)

"""Video: 2 departures from the dock (slippery and grippy floor). The robot docks first (not shown), sits charging with its motors off, then UNDOCK: wheels roll back under it until upright, balance, drive out over the saddle lip, turn and go. Writes results/undock_2runs.mp4.""" import os, math, subprocess os.environ.setdefault("MUJOCO_GL", "osmesa") import numpy as np, mujoco from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont import dock_sim as D from botsim import STATES, CTRL_DT OUT = D.OUT W, H, FPS = 960, 540, 30 OPT = mujoco.MjvOption(); OPT.flags[mujoco.mjtVisFlag.mjVIS_RANGEFINDER] = 0 RUNS = [("Departure 1: slippery floor (friction 0.4)", 0.4, 304), ("Departure 2: grippy floor (friction 1.0)", 1.0, 302)] def main(): D.build_xml() font = ImageFont.load_default(size=26); small = ImageFont.load_default(size=19) fd = OUT / "undock_frames"; fd.mkdir(exist_ok=True) for f in fd.glob("*.png"): f.unlink() n = 0 for title, mu, seed in RUNS: os.environ["FLOOR_MU"] = str(mu) s = D.DockSim(seed=seed, randomize=True); s.seed_ = seed s.place(x=0.30, y=0.0, yaw=0.0); s.hold(0.5); s.run(2.0) p = D.DockPilot(); k = 0 while s.t < 60: # dock (not filmed) if k % 50 == 0: o = s.out m, v, w, lean = p.step(s.t, s.scan(with_intensity=True), (o.x, o.y, o.yaw), STATES[o.state], s.charge, o.pitch, D._ir_bits(s)) s.cmd.mode = D.MODE[m]; s.cmd.v = v; s.cmd.yaw_rate = w if lean: s.cmd.seq = (s.cmd.seq + 1) & 0xFFFF if m in ("done", "failed"): break s.step(); k += 1 print(title, "docked:", p.phase, flush=True) r = mujoco.Renderer(s.m, H, W) cam = mujoco.MjvCamera(); cam.type = mujoco.mjtCamera.mjCAMERA_FREE cam.distance, cam.elevation, cam.azimuth = 0.9, -14, 125 look = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.03]) script = [("Docked, charging, motors off", 1.5, dict(mode=0, v=0.0, yaw_rate=0.0)), ("UNDOCK: wheels roll back under the body", 1.5, dict(mode=5, v=0.0, yaw_rate=0.0, seq=1)), ("Balancing: drive out over the saddle lip", 3.0, dict(mode=0, v=0.15, yaw_rate=0.0)), ("Turn and drive off", 2.0, dict(mode=0, v=0.25, yaw_rate=1.2)), ("Turn and drive off", 2.0, dict(mode=0, v=0.3, yaw_rate=0.0))] stride = int(round(1 / FPS / CTRL_DT)); k = 0; t0 = s.t for cap, secs, cmd in script: for key, v in cmd.items(): if key == "seq": s.cmd.seq = (s.cmd.seq + 1) & 0xFFFF else: setattr(s.cmd, key, v) for _ in range(int(round(secs / CTRL_DT))): o = s.step(); k += 1 if k % stride: continue look = 0.9 * look + 0.1 * np.array([0.5 * s.d.qpos[0], 0.5 * s.d.qpos[1], 0.06]) cam.lookat[:] = look cam.distance = 0.9 * cam.distance + 0.1 * (0.8 + 0.6 * math.hypot(s.d.qpos[0], s.d.qpos[1])) r.update_scene(s.d, cam, OPT) im = Image.fromarray(r.render()); dr = ImageDraw.Draw(im) dr.rectangle([0, 0, W, 78], fill=(255, 255, 255)) dr.text((16, 6), title, fill=(20, 20, 20), font=font) dr.text((16, 44), f"{cap} | {STATES[o.state]:9s} pitch {math.degrees(o.pitch):+5.1f}° speed {o.v:+.2f} m/s " f"{'charging' if s.charge else ''} t {s.t - t0:4.1f} s", fill=(70, 70, 70), font=small) im.save(fd / f"{n:05d}.png"); n += 1 print(title, "end state", STATES[s.out.state], "x", round(float(s.d.qpos[0]), 2), flush=True) r.close(); s.close() subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "error", "-framerate", str(FPS), "-i", str(fd / "%05d.png"), "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "26", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", str(OUT / "undock_2runs.mp4")], check=True) for f in fd.glob("*.png"): f.unlink() if __name__ == "__main__": main()

"""Wobble at standstill + push recovery for cheaper motors (MF5015-V2 10T, Damiao DM-H6215) vs the MF6015. Same robot, same firmware controller (libbot.so). Motor = datasheet Kt/back-EMF/resistance/torque cap/mass/inertia. H6215 has a Hall encoder: 14 pole pairs x 6 Hall states = 84 counts/rev (4.3 deg). Two speed models: 'hall-ok' : drive reports a well-filtered speed (1 dps steps, 5 ms lag) -> optimistic 'hall-raw' : speed = count difference over a 20 ms window -> pessimistic""" import math, sys, numpy as np from multiprocessing import Pool import botsim, motor_compare as mc from botsim import BotSim, LIB, Inputs mc.MOTORS["DM-H6215"] = (0.716, 13.3, 2.5, 2.0, 0.360, 600e-7) # Kt from 320 rpm @ 24 V; inertia estimated CASES = [("MF6015-V2 15T (current)", "abs16"), ("MF5015-V2 10T", "abs16"), ("DM-H6215", "hall-ok"), ("DM-H6215", "hall-raw")] class Sim(BotSim): def __init__(self, enc_mode, **kw): super().__init__(**kw); INS_M3[1] - 1)).center(bx, yy).circle(INS_M3[0] / 2).extrude(INS_M3[1] + 1.5))) return f hd = w.intersect(up(zs, 300)).intersect(cq.Workplane("XY").add(cq.Solid.makeBox(600, 600, DOCK_SPLIT, cq.Vector(-300, -300, 0)))) hd = hd.cut(docked_transform(ring(si - Print flat.""" my, mz = side * MIC_YZ[0], MIC_YZ[1] pc = my - MIC_CHIP_DY # board centre (the port is on MIC_YZ) xs = X_IN_F - 5.0 - 2.0 by, bz = my, mz + MIC_BOSS_DZ plate = box(xs, xs + 2.0, pc - MIC_PCB[0] / 2 - 1, pc + MIC_PCB[0] / 2 + 1, mz - MIC_PCB[1] / 2 - 1, bz + 3.4).edges("|X").fillet(2.5) pcb_back = X_IN_F + MIC_POCKET - 1.5 # Adafruit 6049 PCB is 1.5 mm rib = (cq.Workplane("YZ", origin=(xs + 2.0, 0, 0)).center(pc, mz).rect(MIC_PCB[0] - 0.6, MIC_PCB[1] - 0.6) .rect(MIC_PCB[0] - 4.0, MIC_PCB[1] - 4.0).extrude(pcb_back - xs - 2.0)) plate = plate.union(rib).cut(cyl_x(xs - 1, 4, by, bz, 2.4)) # wire pass over the 6 solder pads (Adafruit 6049: a row along z at 4.61 mm from the mic port) return plate.cut(cq.Workplane("YZ", origin=(xs - 1, 0, 0)).center(my - MIC_PAD_DY, mz - 0.63).rect(5, 15.5).extrude(4)) def build_ir_hood(): """Hood for one TSOP38238 IR receiver, in its local frame (looking along +x, base on the top skin at z = 0). Reads /home/claude/case/wiring_diagram.json, writes wiring_boards.html.""" import json, html, sys sys.path.insert(0, '/home/claude/case') import body_case as _bc bc_ESP_Z, bc_ESP_DY = _bc.ESP_Z, _bc.ESP_DY D = json.load(open('/home/claude/case/wiring_diagram.json')) E = html.escape W, H = 1800, 1290 S = [] # svg pieces (boards) P = {} # (module, pin) -> (x, y, dir) DV = {'l': (-1, 0), 'r': (1, 0), 'u': (0, -1), 'd': (0, 1)} def g(mod, body): S.append(f'<g class="bd" data-m="{E(mod)}">{body}</g>') def rect(x, y, w, h, fill, rx=6, stroke='#0004', extra=''): return f'<rect x="{x}" y="{y}" width="{w}" height="{h}" rx="{rx}" fill="{fill}" stroke="{stroke}" stroke-width="1.2" {extra}/>' def text(x, y, s, size=11, fill='#fff', anchor='start', weight='400', cls=''): return f'<text x="{x}" y="{y}" font-size="{size}" style="fill:{fill}" text-anchor="{anchor}" font-weight="{weight}" class="{cls}">{E(s)}</text>' def title(x, y, s, w=None): return f'<text x="{x}" y="{y}" class="ttl">{E(s)}</text>' def pin(mod, name, x, y, d, label=None, lc='#fff', used=True, shape='sq'): """Header pin / pad at x,y, wire leaves in direction d; label inside the board.""" out = '' if shape == 'sq': out += f'<rect x="{x-4}" y="{y-4}" width="8" height="8" rx="1" fill="#111" stroke="#000"/><rect x="{x-1.6}" y="{y-1.6}" width="3.2" height="3.2" fill="#c9a43c"/>' elif shape == 'pad': out += f'<circle cx="{x}" cy="{y}" r="4.6" fill="#d8b04a" stroke="#7a5a10"/><circle cx="{x}" cy="{y}" r="1.6" fill="#333"/>' elif shape == 'term': out += f'<rect x="{x-7}" y="{y-7}" width="14" height="14" rx="2" fill="#2e7d32" stroke="#0005"/><circle cx="{x}" cy="{y}" r="4" fill="#bbb" stroke="#555"/><line x1="{x-3}" y1="{y}" x2="{x+3}" y2="{y}" stroke="#555" stroke-width="1.4"/>' elif shape == 'none': pass if label is not None: dx, dy = DV[d] if d in 'lr': off = 11 if shape in ('pad','term') else 9 tx, ty, an = x - dx * off, y + 3.5, ('start' if d == 'l' else 'end') out += f'<text x="{tx}" y="{ty}" font-size="9.5" style="fill:{lc}" text-anchor="{an}">{E(label)}</text>' else: tx, ty = x + 3.5, y - dy * 9 an = 'end' if d == 'u' else 'start' out += f'<text x="{tx}" y="{ty}" font-size="9.5" style="fill:{lc}" text-anchor="{an}" transform="rotate(-90 {tx} {ty})">{E(label)}</text>' if used: P[(mod, name)] = (x, y, d) return out # ---------------- left: power ---------------- def battery(x, y): m = "Battery 6S 1400" b = rect(x, y, 200, 96, '#2b4a8b', 10) + rect(x + 6, y + 6, 188, 84, '#33569e', 7, 'none') b += text(x + 14, y + 36, '6S LiPo', 18, '#fff', weight='700') + text(x + 14, y + 56, '1400 mAh · 22.2 V', 12, '#dbe4ff') # leads b += f'<path d="M{x+200} {y+22} H{x+226}" stroke="#d32f2f" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M{x+200} {y+42} H{x+226}" stroke="#222" stroke-width="5"/>' b += rect(x + 226, y + 14, 26, 36, '#f2c200', 3) + text(x + 239, y + 36, 'XT60', 8, '#333', 'middle') b += f'<path d="M{x+200} {y+72} H{x+222}" stroke="#ddd" stroke-width="4"/>' + rect(x + 222, y + 62, 30, 20, '#f4f4f4', 2, '#999') + text(x + 237, y + 75, 'XH', 8, '#333', 'middle') b += pin(m, 'lead +', x + 252, y + 22, 'r', shape='none') + pin(m, 'lead -', x + 252, y + 42, 'r', shape='none') + pin(m, 'balance lead', x + 252, y + 72, 'r', shape='none') b += title(x, y - """Perfboard layout on the 2.54 mm hole grid (component side faces +x, towards the front). Board: standard 5 x 7 cm double-sided FR4, 24 x 18 holes, 70 (robot y) x 50 (robot z), back face at x = X_BACK + BOARD_STANDOFF, centre bc.PB_CENTER. Hole (k, j): y = Y0 + 2.54 k, z = Z0 + 2.54 j (k 0..23, j 0..17). Regions: the ESP32 DevKit sits on two 22-pin female header rows (j 8 and j 17) over y -60..-4; under it there is 8.5 mm of height for flat parts (74AHCT125, resistors). The CAN board stands on spacers at y -64..-31, z 81-91. Plugs go in the free area below the DevKit (y -31..+6, z 77..98). """ import body_case as bc XB = bc.X_BACK + bc.BOARD_STANDOFF # board back face XF = XB + 1.6 # component face CY, CZ = bc.PB_CENTER NK, NJ = 24, 18 # standard 5 x 7 cm board: 24 x 18 holes (432), 2.54 mm, centred Y0 = CY - (NK - 1) * 2.54 / 2 # hole k = 0 at the -Y end (5.8 mm from the edge) Z0 = CZ - (NJ - 1) * 2.54 / 2 # hole j = 0 at the bottom (3.4 mm from the edge) DK_COLS, DK_ROWS = (1, 22), (8, 17) # DevKit female headers: holes k 1-22 on rows j 8 and 17 def hole(k, j): assert 0 <= k < NK and 0 <= j < NJ, (k, j) return (Y0 + 2.54 * k, Z0 + 2.54 * j) # plugs: name -> (k of pin 1, j, pins, pitch in holes, height, kind). Rows j 0 and 3 stay at k >= 12, clear of the # CAN board standing on spacers over k 0-11 (y -64..-31, z 81-91). PLUGS = { "J2": (12, 0, 4, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J1": (18, 0, 2, 2, 8.0, "XT30PW right-angle PCB plug (15 A)"), "J7": (12, 3, 3, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J5": (17, 3, 5, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J3": (1, 6, 4, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J4": (6, 6, 3, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J6": (10, 6, 5, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), "J8": (16, 6, 6, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), # IR receivers: 3V3, GND, GPIO13-16 "J9": (22, 6, 1, 1, 8.5, "2.54 header + Dupont"), # power switch OFF: GPIO21 (100 k pull-down on the board) } def plug_pin(name, i): k, j, n, p, h, _ = PLUGS[name] y, z = hole(k + i * p, j) return (XF + h, y, z) # wire end = top of the housing def plug_box(name): k, j, n, p, h, kind = PLUGS[name] y1, z = hole(k, j); y2, _ = hole(k + (n - 1) * p, j) if kind.startswith("XT30"): return (XF, XF + h, (y1 + y2) / 2 - 5.1, (y1 + y2) / 2 + 5.1, z - 2.6, z + 2.6) return (XF, XF + h, y1 - 1.27, y2 + 1.27, z - 2.5, z + 2.5) # flat parts: name -> (k1, j1, k2, j2, height, what). Resistors 1/4 W lying flat, leads 10.16 mm apart (4 holes); # all of them and the 74AHCT125 sit under the DevKit (rows 9-16 are free between its header rows, 8.5 mm of height). PARTS = { "U1 74AHCT125 (DIP-14)": (8, 11, 14, 14, 4.5, "Pi MOSI -> 5 V WS2812 data; 1OE to GND, unused inputs to GND"), "R4 100k (VBAT top)": (1, 10, 5, 10, 2.5, "J7-1 -> GPIO1"), "R5 12k (VBAT bottom)": (1, 11, 5, 11, 2.5, "GPIO1 -> GND"), "R6 100k (dock top)": (1, 12, 5, 12, 2.5, "J7-2 -> GPIO6"), "R7 12k (dock bottom)": (1, 13, 5, 13, 2.5, "GPIO6 -> GND"), "R8 56k (USB top)": (1, 14, 5, 14, 2.5, "J7-3 -> GPIO7"), "R9 10k (USB bottom)": (1, 15, 5, 15, 2.5, "GPIO7 -> GND"), "R2 1k (echo top)": (16, 10, 20, 10, 2.5, "J2-3 -> GPIO11"), "R3 2k (echo bottom)": (16, 11, 20, 11, 2.5, "GPIO11 -> GND"), "R1 330 (eye data)": (16, 12, 20, 12, 2.5, "U1 1Y -> J4-2"), "R10 330 (LED R)": (16, 13, 20, 13, 2.5, "GPIO38 -> J6-2"), "R11 330 (LED G)": (16, 14, 20, 14, 2.5, "GPIO39 -> J6-3"), "R12 330 (LED B)": (16, 15, 20, 15, 2.5, "GPIO40 -> J6-4"), "C1 470 uF 10 V (6.3 x 11)": (22, 0, 23, 0, 11.0, "5 V bus, beside the 5 V input plug J1 (was under J8)"), } def part_box(name): k1, j1, k2, j2, h, _ = PARTS[name] y1, z1 = hole(k1, j1); y2, z2 = hole(k2, j2) if name.startswith("C1"): c = ((y1 + y2) / 2, z1) return (XF, XF + h, c[0] - 3.2, c[0] + 3.2, c[1] - 3.2, c[1] + 3.2) return (XF, XF + h, min(y1, y2) - 1.2, max(y1, y2) + 1.2, min(z1, z2) - 1.2, max(z1, z2) + 1.2)

"""Bought parts as real 3D models, placed in the robot frame (x forward, y left, z up, origin on the axle). Every part says where its geometry comes from: STEP - manufacturer / published model, downloaded (models/bought/) DRAW - built here from the official mechanical drawing (models/drawings/) LIST - outer envelope from the seller's listed dimensions (no model published): a box, labelled as such """ import math, cadquery as cq import body_case as bc from load_models import load AX = {"x": 0, "y": 1, "z": 2} def orient(shape, xr, yr, zr): """Rigid rotation: robot x = model axis xr (e.g. '-z'), etc. Must be a proper rotation.""" rows = [] for a in (xr, yr, zr): r = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]; r[AX[a[-1]]] = -1.0 if a[0] == "-" else 1.0; rows.append(r) det = (rows[0][0] * (rows[1][1] * rows[2][2] - rows[1][2] * rows[2][1]) - rows[0][1] * (rows[1][0] * rows[2][2] - rows[1][2] * rows[2][0]) + rows[0][2] * (rows[1][0] * rows[2][1] - rows[1][1] * rows[2][0])) assert abs(det - 1) < 1e-9, (xr, yr, zr) from OCP.gp import gp_Trsf from OCP.BRepBuilderAPI import BRepBuilderAPI_Transform t = gp_Trsf() t.SetValues(rows[0][0], rows[0][1], rows[0][2], 0, rows[1][0], rows[1][1], rows[1][2], 0, rows[2][0], rows[2][1], rows[2][2], 0) out = cq.Shape.cast(BRepBuilderAPI_Transform(shape.wrapped, t, True).Shape()) return out, (lambda p: tuple(sum(rows[i][j] * p[j] for j in range(3)) for i in range(3))) PLACE = {} # name -> (axes, ref_model, target): to map model-frame pin positions to the robot frame def to_robot(name, p): axes, ref, tgt = PLACE[name] _, R = orient(cq.Solid.makeBox(1, 1, 1), *axes) a, r = R(p), R(ref) return tuple(tgt[i] + a[i] - r[i] for i in range(3)) def place(shape, axes, ref_model, target, name=None): if name: PLACE[name] = (axes, ref_model, target) s, R = orient(shape, *axes) r = R(ref_model) return s.translate((target[0] - r[0], target[1] - r[1], target[2] - r[2])) def box(x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1): return cq.Solid.makeBox(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, z1 - z0, cq.Vector(x0, y0, z0)) def cyl(p, d, h, axis): # cylinder from point p along +axis return cq.Solid.makeCylinder(d / 2, h, cq.Vector(*p), cq.Vector(*axis)) # ---------------- built from official drawings ---------------- def pi_zero_2w(header=True): """Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, from the official mechanical drawing (RP-008358): 65 x 30 PCB, holes 3.5 in, 58 x 23, 2x20 GPIO header centred 32.5 from the left / 3.5 from the top edge, mini-HDMI at 12.4, micro-USB at 41.4 and 54 on the bottom edge, CSI on the right end. """Parametric MF6015 -> 12 mm hex RC wheel adapter (CadQuery). Print orientation: hex end DOWN on the bed. The 45-degree cone under the flange means no supports are needed, and the motor-facing flange and centering spigot come out as clean top surfaces. Run: python3 wheel_adapter.py -> writes STEP + STL next to this script. """ import cadquery as cq import math, pathlib # ---------------- motor interface (from LKMTECH MF6015 v2 drawing + STEP) ------ BORE_D = 12.7 # motor centering bore, H7 (1/2") SPIGOT_D = 12.6 # printed spigot: tune 12.55-12.70 for a snug slide fit SPIGOT_L = 4.0 # bore is ~17 mm deep, 4 mm is plenty for centering PCD = 25.0 # 4 x M3 bolt circle M3_CLEAR = 3.4 M3_HEAD_CB = 6.0 # counterbore for M3 socket head (5.5 mm head) # ---------------- adapter body ------------------------------------------------- FLANGE_D = 36.0 FLANGE_T = 5.5 # plate under screw heads. M3x8 -> 2.5 mm into motor NECK_D = 18.0 NECK_L = 6.0 # standoff so the wheel clears the motor - set per wheel HEX_AF = 11.95 # 12 mm hex across flats, minus a print tolerance HEX_L = 7.0 # match the depth of your wheel's hex pocket (it must bottom out) M4_INSERT_D = 5.6 # hole for M4 heat-set insert (check your insert's spec) M4_INSERT_L = 9.0 CHAMFER = 0.6 BRIDGE_LAYER = 0.2 # layer height used by the two-layer bridge at the screw-head seats CONE_H = (FLANGE_D - NECK_D) / 2 # 45 degrees -> support-free def build(): # z = 0 is the motor mating face; +z goes into the motor, -z toward the wheel. spigot = (cq.Workplane("XY").circle(SPIGOT_D / 2).extrude(SPIGOT_L) .faces(">Z").edges().chamfer(0.8)) flange = cq.Workplane("XY").circle(FLANGE_D / 2).extrude(-FLANGE_T) cone = (cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=-FLANGE_T) .circle(FLANGE_D / 2).workplane(offset=-CONE_H) .circle(NECK_D / 2).loft()) z0 = -FLANGE_T - CONE_H neck = cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=z0).circle(NECK_D / 2).extrude(-NECK_L) z1 = z0 - NECK_L hexp = (cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=z1) .polygon(6, HEX_AF / math.cos(math.radians(30))).extrude(-HEX_L) .faces("<Z").edges().chamfer(CHAMFER)) body = spigot.union(flange).union(cone).union(neck).union(hexp) zb = z1 - HEX_L # M4 heat-set insert from the hex end, with a 45 deg pointed end (prints without a bridge, hex-down) body = body.cut(cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=zb) .circle(M4_INSERT_D / 2).extrude(M4_INSERT_L)) body = body.cut(cq.Solid.makeCone(M4_INSERT_D / 2, 0.01, M4_INSERT_D / 2, cq.Vector(0, 0, zb + M4_INSERT_L), cq.Vector(0, 0, 1))) # 4 x M3 clearance holes + counterbores opening on the wheel side. The head seat is printed with the # two-layer bridge trick (hex-down): layer 1 leaves a slot as wide as the hole, layer 2 a square, then the round # hole: clean bridges, no sacrificial membrane to drill out, no support. pts_a = [(a, PCD / 2 * math.cos(math.radians(a)), PCD / 2 * math.sin(math.radians(a))) for a in (45, 135, 225, 315)] pts = [(x, y) for _, x, y in pts_a] seat = -FLANGE_T body = body.cut(cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=seat + 2 * BRIDGE_LAYER) .pushPoints(pts).circle(M3_CLEAR / 2).extrude(FLANGE_T + 1)) for a, x, y in pts_a: slot = (cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=seat).center(x, y) .rect(M3_HEAD_CB + 0.4, M3_CLEAR).extrude(BRIDGE_LAYER).rotate((x, y, 0), (x, y, 1), a)) sq = (cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=seat + BRIDGE_LAYER).center(x, y) .rect(M3_CLEAR, M3_CLEAR).extrude(BRIDGE_LAYER + 0.01).rotate((x, y, 0), (x, y, 1), a)) body = body.cut(slot.intersect(cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=seat).center(x, y).circle(M3_HEAD_CB / 2).extrude(BRIDGE_LAYER))).cut(sq) body = body.cut(cq.Workplane("XY").workplane(offset=seat) .pushPoints(pts).circle(M3_HEAD_CB / 2).extrude(-(CONE_H + 1))) # outer edge chamfer on the mating flange return body if __name__ == "__main__": out = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent part = build() cq.exporters.export(part, str(out / "mf6015_hex12_adapter.step")) cq.exporters.export(part, str(out / "mf6015_hex12_adapter.stl"), tolerance=0.02, angularTolerance=0.1) bb = part.val().BoundingBox() print("length %.1f mm, volume %.1f cm3, PETG mass ~%.0f g" % (bb.zlen, part.val().Volume() / 1000, part.val().Volume() / 1000 * 1.27))

# Testing the CAN driver and code Three levels, cheapest first. Do them in order: each one rules out a class of problems before the next. ## 1. Unit tests on the PC (no hardware) ``` firmware/esp32/test_host/run_tests.sh ``` Builds `src/lk_motor.cpp` unchanged with g++ against a fake ESP-IDF TWAI driver and feeds it LK frames. 54 checks: torque packing in the 0x280 frame (motor 1 bytes 0-1, motor 2 mirrored, clamp ±2048), reply parsing (temperature, current, speed, direction), the 0x88/0x80 echoes and foreign IDs ignored, encoder unwrap forwards and backwards for 14/15/16-bit encoders, range detection from the wrap and from the speed ratio, a 100 ms reply gap while the wheel keeps turning, the CAN timeout (including a reply stamped after `now`), a full TX queue never blocking. They found two problems, both fixed: motion before the encoder range is known was counted at the 16-bit guess (now learned after 90° instead of 180°: at most a 1.2 rad one-off offset, no jump), and a reply gap could be taken for an encoder wrap and switch the range (now unwrapped using the reported speed). ## 2. Bench with a USB-CAN adapter (no motors, no battery) Hardware: the ESP32-S3 DevKit + the Waveshare CAN board wired as on the robot (GPIO4 -> CTX, GPIO5 -> CRX, 3.3 V, GND) and a USB-CAN adapter: a candleLight / CANable (gs_usb firmware, ~€15-30) works on Linux (SocketCAN), macOS and Windows (`gs_usb`); a CANable with slcan firmware works everywhere (`slcan:`). Adapter CAN_H/CAN_L/GND to the CAN board's H/L/GND, termination ON at the adapter (the CAN board has its own 120 ohm): ~60 ohm between H and L. ``` pip install python-can pyserial mujoco numpy # + gs_usb on macOS/Windows with a candleLight sudo ip link set can0 up type can bitrate 1000000 # Linux SocketCAN only ``` ### 2a. Transceiver self-test and bus scan (CAN probe firmware) ``` cd firmware/esp32 && pio run -e esp32s3_canprobe -t upload && pio device monitor -e esp32s3_canprobe ``` Prints `self-test: 20/20 frames came back through the transceiver`: the ESP32 sends frames to itself through the SN65HVD230 (no other node needed). 0/20 = CTX/CRX swapped, no 3.3 V or a bad joint. Then it scans IDs 1-4 every 2 s. ### 2b. Watch the robot firmware's traffic Flash the robot firmware (`pio run -e esp32s3 -t upload`) and run ``` python3 bench/can_monitor.py socketcan:can0 ``` Disarmed: 0x9C requests to 0x141/0x142 at ~480/s each, with a 0x80 every 50 ms; nothing answers yet (the adapter ACKs the frames). Error frames must stay at 0. The adapter must be the only extra node. ### 2c. The robot firmware against two virtual motors over the real bus ``` cd firmware/esp32 && pio run -e esp32s3_bench -t upload # robot firmware, IMU from the PC python3 bench/bench_hil.py --serial /dev/ttyUSB0 --can socketcan:can0 ``` `esp32s3_bench` is the robot firmware with the real TWAI driver; only the IMU comes from the PC (DevKit **UART** USB port, 921600, the Pi's arm/drive commands share it). The PC plays motors 1 and 2 on the real bus, runs the physics and feeds the IMU, so the robot stands up, balances, drives, gets pushed - with the real CAN driver, transceiver, wiring, termination and 1 Mbit/s timing. Same scenarios and output as the QEMU test (`hil/run_hil.py`). `can_loss` mutes the virtual motors for 100 ms; also pull the CAN cable by hand while it balances: the firmware must log `motor fault: no CAN reply for ~20 ms`, disarm, and keep sending 0x80. `bench/test_bench.py` checks the kit itself without hardware (virtual CAN bus + the bench build in QEMU). ## 3. One real motor, wheel off the ground 1. With LK's PC tool on the motor's UART connector: ID 1 (left) or 2 (right), CAN 1 Mbit/s. 2. Motor on its supply (or the battery through the 30 A fuse), CAN board H/L to the motor, 60 ohm H-L with power off. 3. CAN probe firmware (2a): the scan must show `motor 1: state ... enc ...`. 4. `e`: turn the wheel one full turn by hand -> counts per turn (cross-check of the firmware's own detection). 5. `+`: 0.2 N·m for 0.5 s. If the wheel turned so the robot would roll forward, keep `DIR_LEFT = +1`, else -1. Same with `2` for the right motor and `DIR_RIGHT`. 6. Only then the robot firmware: boot log `encoder range detected: N counts/turn` once the wheel has turned.

"""Bench test over a REAL CAN bus: the real ESP32-S3 (firmware env esp32s3_bench) and its CAN board talk to two virtual LK motors that this PC plays through a USB-CAN adapter; the robot's physics (MuJoCo) runs here and feeds the IMU over the DevKit's "UART" USB port. Same scenarios as hil/run_hil.py (QEMU), but with the real TWAI driver, transceiver, wiring, termination and timing. python3 bench_hil.py --serial /dev/ttyUSB0 --can socketcan:can0 [scenario ...] [--seeds 1,2,3] scenarios: standup_face standup_back balance_push drive cmd_timeout can_loss (default: all) Wiring: DevKit "UART" port -> PC (serial), CAN board H/L -> adapter CAN_H/CAN_L + GND, 120 ohm at the adapter end (most adapters have a switch/jumper) and the 120 ohm already on the Waveshare board. No motors, no battery needed. """ import argparse, json, os, pathlib, struct, sys, threading, time import numpy as np HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent ROOT = HERE.parent sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "hil")); sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "pi")); sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE)) import run_hil # noqa: E402 (scenarios) from lkbus import Plant, VirtualLK, crc as sim_crc, frame as sim_frame, CTRL_DT # noqa: E402 from robot.link import (Telemetry, TELEM_FMT, MSG_TELEM, MSG_EVENT, CMD_FMT, MSG_CMD, F_ARM, F_DISARM, # noqa: E402 F_AUTO_STANDUP, F_OBST_STOP, MODE_VELOCITY, crc8 as pi_crc, frame as pi_frame) from canbus import open_bus # noqa: E402 CFG = dict(serial=None, can=None, reset=True) class BenchLink: """The Pi's side of the link, on the same serial port as the IMU frames.""" def __init__(self, host): self.h = host; self.telem = Telemetry(); self.seq = 0 def send(self, v=0.0, yaw_rate=0.0, mode=MODE_VELOCITY, angle=0.0, arm=False, disarm=False, auto_standup=True, obstacle_stop=True, new_turn=False): if new_turn: self.seq = (self.seq + 1) & 0xFFFF flags = (F_ARM if arm else 0) | (F_DISARM if disarm else 0) | (F_AUTO_STANDUP if auto_standup else 0) | (F_OBST_STOP if obstacle_stop else 0) self.h.write(pi_frame(MSG_CMD, struct.pack(CMD_FMT, mode, flags, self.seq, float(v), float(yaw_rate), float(angle)))) class _Alive: def poll(self): return None class BenchHost: """Drop-in for run_hil.Host: same attributes the scenarios use.""" def __init__(self, seed=1, randomize=True, log_dir="/tmp/bench"): import serial self.plant = Plant(seed, randomize) self.vlk = VirtualLK(self.plant) self.lock = threading.Lock(); self.wlock = threading.Lock() self.log_dir = pathlib.Path(log_dir); self.log_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True) self.can_mute_until = -1.0 self.events = []; self.telem = []; self.cycles = 0; self.dts = []; self.host_ms = []; self.wall = [] self.stop = False; self.q = _Alive() self.ser = serial.serial_for_url(CFG["serial"], baudrate=921600, timeout=0.01) self.bus = open_bus(CFG["can"]) self.link = BenchLink(self) self.can_rx = 0; self.can_tx = 0; self.can_errors = 0 def write(self, b): with self.wlock: self.ser.write(b) def start(self, tag): self.tag = tag self.con = open(self.log_dir / f"{tag}_console.log", "wb") threading.Thread(target=self.serial_loop, daemon=True).start() # listening before the ESP32 boots threading.Thread(target=self.can_loop, daemon=True).start() if CFG["reset"] and hasattr(self.ser, "rts"): try: # DevKit auto-reset: RTS -> EN, DTR -> IO0 (keep high) self.ser.dtr = False; self.ser.rts = True; time.sleep(0.1); self.ser.rts = False except Exception: pass def close(self): self.stop = True; time.sleep(0.05) for f in (self.ser.close, self.bus.shutdown, self.con.close): try: f() except Exception: pass print(f" CAN: {self.can_rx} frames from the ESP32, {self.can_tx} replies, {self.can_errors} error frames") # -------------------------------------------------- real CAN: the two virtual motors def can_loop(self): import can while not self.stop: try: m = self.bus.recv(0.01) except Exception: break if m is None: continue if m.is_error_frame: self.can_errors += 1; continue self.can_rx += 1 with self.lock: self.vlk.mute_until = self.can_mute_until out = self.vlk.handle(m.arbitration_id, m.data) for i, d in out: try: self.bus.send(can.Message(arbitration_id=i, data=d, is_extended_id=False)); self.can_tx += 1 except Exception: pass # -------------------------------------------------- serial: IMU lock-step + Pi frames + console text def serial_loop(self): buf = bytearray(); P = self.plant while not self.stop: try: data = self.ser.read(max(1, self.ser.in_waiting)) # return as soon as bytes arrive (not after 512 / timeout) except Exception: break if not data: continue buf += data while True: i = buf.find(b"\xA5\x5A") if i < 0: self.con.write(bytes(buf[:-1])); del buf[:-1]; break if i: self.con.write(bytes(buf[:i])); del buf[:i] if len(buf) < 4: break n = 4 + buf[3] + 1 if len(buf) < n: break body = bytes(buf[2:n - 1]); c = buf[n - 1]; t, p = body[0], body[2:] if t in (MSG_TELEM, MSG_EVENT) and pi_crc(body) == c: if t == MSG_TELEM and len(p) == struct.calcsize(TELEM_FMT): self.link.telem = Telemetry.unpack(p) elif t == MSG_EVENT: self.events.append((P.t, p.decode(errors="replace"))) del buf[:n]; continue if t == ord("S") and sim_crc(body) == c: t_us, = struct.unpack("<I", p) w0 = time.perf_counter() with self.lock: dt = CTRL_DT if P.t_fw is None else ((t_us - P.t_fw) & 0xFFFFFFFF) * 1e-6 P.t_fw = t_us if self.cycles > 0: P.advance(min(dt, 0.05)); self.dts.append(dt) self.cycles += 1 imu = P.imu() self.write(sim_frame(ord("I"), imu)) self.host_ms.append(1e3 * (time.perf_counter() - w0)) del buf[:n]; continue del buf[:2] # not a frame: resync # -------------------------------------------------- scenario API (same as run_hil.Host) def run_for(self, seconds, **cmd): t_end = self.plant.t + seconds; deadline = time.time() + seconds * 5 + 20 while self.plant.t < t_end and time.time() < deadline: if cmd.get("silent") is not True: self.link.send(**{k: v for k, v in cmd.items() if k != "silent"}) self.telem.append((self.plant.t, self.link.telem)) time.sleep(0.05) return self.plant.t >= t_end def wait_boot(self, timeout=15): t0 = time.time() while time.time() - t0 < timeout: if any("state" in e for _, e in self.events): return True time.sleep(0.05) return False def main(): ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter) ap.add_argument("--serial", required=True, help="DevKit UART port, e.g. /dev/ttyUSB0, COM4, socket://host:port") ap.add_argument("--can", required=True, help="adapter, e.g. socketcan:can0, gs_usb:0, slcan:/dev/ttyACM0 (see canbus.py)") ap.add_argument("--seeds", default="1") ap.add_argument("--no-reset", action="store_true", help="don't reset the ESP32 through RTS before each scenario") ap.add_argument("--out", default="bench_results.json") ap.add_argument("scenarios", nargs="*") a = ap.parse_args() CFG.update(serial=a.serial, can=a.can, reset=not a.no_reset) run_hil.Host = BenchHost # the scenarios now drive the real ESP32 names = a.scenarios or list(run_hil.SCEN) res = {} for n in names: for s in [int(x) for x in a.seeds.split(",")]: t0 = time.time(); r = run_hil.SCEN[n](s); r["wall_s"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1) res[f"{n}_{s}"] = r print(n, s, json.dumps(r), flush=True) pathlib.Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(res, indent=1)) if __name__ == "__main__": main()

"""Watch the robot's CAN bus and decode the LK traffic, once per second. python3 can_monitor.py socketcan:can0 (see canbus.py for other adapters) Per second: frames per ID, the torque the ESP32 commands (0x280, in N·m per motor), the motors' replies (temperature, current, speed, encoder), error frames and the bus load. What to expect from the robot firmware: disarmed : 0x141/0x142 0x9C requests at ~480/s each, every 25th cycle 0x80 instead; replies 0x9C from both motors armed : 0x280 torque at 500/s + 0xA1 replies from 0x141 and 0x142 at 500/s each bus load : ~40 % armed at 1 Mbit/s (3 frames per 2 ms) """ import collections, struct, sys, time from canbus import open_bus KT, IQ_FULL, IQ_MAX = 0.14, 16.5, 2048 BITS_PER_FRAME = 130 # standard 8-byte frame incl. typical bit stuffing def iq_nm(v): return v * IQ_FULL / IQ_MAX * KT def main(spec, seconds=None): bus = open_bus(spec) t0 = last = time.time() cnt = collections.Counter(); errs = 0; latest = {}; total = 0 print(f"listening on {spec} (Ctrl-C to stop)") try: while seconds is None or time.time() - t0 < seconds: m = bus.recv(0.05) if m is not None: total += 1 if m.is_error_frame: errs += 1 else: cmd = m.data[0] if m.dlc else None cnt[(m.arbitration_id, cmd if m.arbitration_id != 0x280 else "iq")] += 1 latest[(m.arbitration_id, cmd)] = bytes(m.data) if time.time() - last >= 1.0: dt = time.time() - last; last = time.time() line = [f"{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} load {100 * sum(cnt.values()) * BITS_PER_FRAME / 1e6 / dt:4.1f} % errors {errs}"] for (i, c), n in sorted(cnt.items(), key=lambda x: (x[0][0], str(x[0][1]))): tag = "torque 0x280" if i == 0x280 else f"0x{i:03X} {c:#04x}" line.append(f" {tag}: {n / dt:5.0f}/s") for (i, c), d in sorted(latest.items(), key=lambda x: (x[0][0], x[0][1] or 0)): if i == 0x280 and len(d) >= 4: a, b = struct.unpack("<hh", d[:4]); line.append(f" cmd: motor1 {iq_nm(a):+.3f} N·m motor2 {iq_nm(b):+.3f} N·m") elif c in (0x9C, 0xA1) and len(d) == 8 and 0x140 < i < 0x145: t, iq, dps, enc = struct.unpack("<bhhH", d[1:]) line.append(f" motor {i - 0x140}: {t} C {iq * IQ_FULL / IQ_MAX:+.2f} A {dps:+5d} dps enc {enc}") print("\n".join(line), flush=True) cnt.clear(); errs = 0; latest.clear() except KeyboardInterrupt: pass finally: bus.shutdown() return total if __name__ == "__main__": if len(sys.argv) < 2: print(__doc__); sys.exit(1) main(sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)

"""Open a CAN adapter with python-can from a short spec string. socketcan:can0 Linux SocketCAN (candleLight/CANable with gs_usb firmware, PEAK, Kvaser...): first `sudo ip link set can0 up type can bitrate 1000000` gs_usb:0 candleLight/CANable (gs_usb firmware) directly over libusb (macOS, Windows): pip install gs_usb slcan:/dev/ttyACM0 CANable with slcan firmware (any OS), e.g. slcan:COM5 on Windows pcan:PCAN_USBBUS1 PEAK PCAN-USB virtual:test python-can's in-process virtual bus (tests) """ import can BITRATE = 1_000_000 def open_bus(spec): kind, _, chan = spec.partition(":") kw = dict(interface=kind, channel=chan or None) if kind == "gs_usb": kw["channel"] = int(chan or 0); kw["index"] = int(chan or 0); kw["bitrate"] = BITRATE elif kind in ("slcan", "pcan", "kvaser", "ixxat", "vector"): kw["bitrate"] = BITRATE elif kind == "virtual": kw["receive_own_messages"] = False return can.Bus(**kw)

"""Self-test of the bench kit without hardware. 1. CAN side: BenchHost's virtual motors on python-can's in-process virtual bus; a second bus endpoint plays the ESP32 and sends the robot firmware's frames (0x9C, 0x88, 0x280, 0x80, 0xA1); replies are checked byte by byte. 2. Serial side: the bench firmware (env esp32s3_bench_qemu = esp32s3_bench with DIO flash) runs in QEMU; bench_hil talks to its UART0 over TCP exactly as it would over the DevKit's USB-UART: IMU lock-step, Pi command frames (arm) in, telemetry + events out. QEMU has no CAN bus, so the motors never answer: the firmware must arm, try to switch the motors on and report a motor fault (that is the expected end state here). Run: python3 test_bench.py (part 2 needs QEMU + /tmp/flash_bench.bin, see bench/README.md) """ import os, socket, struct, subprocess, sys, time, pathlib HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE)); sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent / "hil")) import can import bench_hil as B from lkbus import ID_L, ID_R, ID_MULTI, DIR, IQ_MAX fails = 0 def check(c, msg): global fails print((" ok " if c else " FAIL ") + msg) if not c: fails += 1 def can_side(): print("1. virtual motors on a python-can bus") B.CFG.update(serial="loop://", can="virtual:benchtest", reset=False) h = B.BenchHost(seed=3); h.plant.place(0) h.start("cantest") esp = can.Bus(interface="virtual", channel="benchtest") def xfer(i, d, n): esp.send(can.Message(arbitration_id=i, data=bytes(d), is_extended_id=False)) out = [] t0 = time.time() while len(out) < n and time.time() - t0 < 1: m = esp.recv(0.1) if m: out.append(m) return out r = xfer(ID_L, [0x9C, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], 1) check(len(r) == 1 and r[0].arbitration_id == ID_L and r[0].data[0] == 0x9C and r[0].dlc == 8, "0x9C read state -> one 0x9C reply from 0x141") r = xfer(ID_R, [0x88, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], 1) check(len(r) == 1 and bytes(r[0].data) == bytes([0x88] + [0] * 7) and h.plant.on[ID_R], "0x88 -> echo of the command, motor 2 on") r = xfer(ID_L, [0x88, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], 1) r = xfer(ID_MULTI, list(struct.pack("<hhhh", 300, -300, 0, 0)), 2) ids = sorted(m.arbitration_id for m in r) check(ids == [ID_L, ID_R] and all(m.data[0] == 0xA1 for m in r), "0x280 -> 0xA1 replies from 0x141 and 0x142") check(h.plant.iq_cmd[ID_L] == 300 and h.plant.iq_cmd[ID_R] == -300, "0x280 iq applied to motor 1 / motor 2") rep = {m.arbitration_id: struct.unpack("<BbhhH", bytes(m.data)) for m in r} check(rep[ID_L][2] == 300 and rep[ID_R][2] == -300, "reply iq = commanded iq") xfer(ID_MULTI, list(struct.pack("<hhhh", 5000, -5000, 0, 0)), 2) check(h.plant.iq_cmd[ID_L] == IQ_MAX and h.plant.iq_cmd[ID_R] == -IQ_MAX, "iq clamped to +-2048") r = xfer(ID_L, [0x80, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], 1) check(len(r) == 1 and r[0].data[0] == 0x80 and not h.plant.on[ID_L] and h.plant.iq_cmd[ID_L] == 0, "0x80 -> echo, motor 1 off, torque 0") h.can_mute_until = h.plant.t + 10 r = xfer(ID_L, [0x9C, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], 1) check(len(r) == 0, "muted (CAN unplugged): no reply") esp.shutdown(); h.close() def serial_side(): print("2. bench firmware in QEMU <-> bench_hil over UART0") flash = "/tmp/flash_bench.bin" if not os.path.exists(flash): print(" skipped: build env esp32s3_bench_qemu into /tmp/flash_bench.bin first"); return s = socket.socket(); s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)); port = s.getsockname()[1]; s.close() q = subprocess.Popen([os.environ.get("QEMU", "/opt/dl/qemu/qemu/bin/qemu-system-xtensa"), "-nographic", "-accel", "tcg", "-machine", "esp32s3", "-icount", "shift=2,sleep=on,align=off", "-m", "8M", "-global", "ssi_psram.is_octal=true", "-global", "ssi_psram.size_mbytes=8", "-drive", f"file={flash},if=mtd,format=raw", "-serial", f"tcp:127.0.0.1:{port},server=on,wait=on,nodelay=on", "-monitor", "none"], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL) time.sleep(1.0) try: B.CFG.update(serial=f"socket://127.0.0.1:{port}", can="virtual:qemutest", reset=False) h = B.BenchHost(seed=1); h.plant.place(0); h.plant.hold = h.plant.d.qpos.copy() h.start("serialtest") booted = h.wait_boot(60) check(booted, "boot: IMU answered over the shared port, state event received as a Pi frame") h.run_for(0.4, arm=False) cyc0 = h.cycles h.run_for(1.0, arm=True) import numpy as np d = np.array(h.dts[-200:]) if h.dts else np.array([0]) check(h.cycles - cyc0 > 300, f"lock-step running: {h.cycles - cyc0} control cycles in 1 s of robot time") check(abs(float(np.median(d)) - 0.002) < 0.0002, f"control period {1e3 * float(np.median(d)):.2f} ms") check(h.link.telem.t_ms > 0, f"telemetry frames parsed (t_ms {h.link.telem.t_ms})") check(h.link.telem.armed, "arm command reached the firmware (armed flag in telemetry)") ev = " | ".join(e for _, e in h.events) check("motor fault" in ev, "no motors on the bus -> firmware reports a CAN motor fault: " + ev[-160:]) h.close() finally: q.terminate(); q.wait(5) if __name__ == "__main__": can_side() serial_side() print(f"\n{'all passed' if not fails else f'{fails} FAILED'}") sys.exit(1 if fails else 0)

"""CAN bus load / timing and ground offset between the ESP32's CAN transceiver and the motors' CAN reference. Lengths and gauges come from the harness model (case/wiring_data.json).""" import json WD = json.load(open("/home/claude/case/wiring_data.json")) OHM_PER_M = {12: 0.00521, 16: 0.0132, 20: 0.0333, 22: 0.0530, 24: 0.0842, 26: 0.134} def wire(h, sig): for x in WD: if x["name"] == h: for c in x["conds"]: if c["sig"] == sig: return c["L"] / 100 * OHM_PER_M[c["awg"]], c["L"], c["awg"] raise KeyError((h, sig)) out = {} # ---- CAN timing (1 Mbit/s, standard 11-bit frames, 8 data bytes) ---- BIT = 1e-6 def frame_bits(n=8, worst=True): base = 47 + 8 * n # SOF..EOF incl. CRC delimiter, ACK, EOF (no IFS) stuff = (34 + 8 * n - 1) // 4 if worst else 0 return base + stuff + 3 # + intermission CYCLE = 0.002 # control period (500 Hz) f = frame_bits() on = 3 * f * BIT # 0x280 torque frame + 2 replies off = 4 * f * BIT # 2 x 0x9C + 2 replies (motors off) out["can"] = dict(frame_us_worst=round(f * BIT * 1e6), per_cycle_on_us=round(on * 1e6), load_on_pct=round(100 * on / CYCLE), per_cycle_off_us=round(off * 1e6), load_off_pct=round(100 * off / CYCLE), retransmits_that_fit_in_a_cycle=int((CYCLE - on) / ((frame_bits() + 23) * BIT)), bus_off_recovery_ms=round(128 * 11 * BIT * 1e3, 2), can_timeout_ms=20, note="Replies are read at the start of the next cycle (1 cycle of latency, modelled in the sim). " "A bus-off costs ~1.4 ms + one cycle: below the 20 ms CAN timeout, so the robot keeps balancing.") # ---- ground offset: transceiver GND vs motor V- (the motors' CAN reference; the bus has no ground wire) ---- I_MOTOR_PEAK, I_5V_PEAK, I_REG_IN = 16.5, 4.66, 1.2 r_mot = wire("PDB -> motor L power", "V-")[0] r_j1 = wire("5 V regulator -> perfboard J1", "GND")[0] r_reg = wire("PDB -> 5 V regulator", "GND")[0] R_CONTACTS = 0.002 # XT30 + solder joints + PDB copper (estimate) v_motor = I_MOTOR_PEAK * (r_mot + 0.0005) v_board = I_5V_PEAK * (r_j1 + R_CONTACTS) + (I_REG_IN + I_5V_PEAK) * r_reg out["ground"] = dict(motor_return_mOhm=round(r_mot * 1e3, 2), perfboard_gnd_mOhm=round(r_j1 * 1e3, 2), worst_offset_mV=round((v_motor + v_board) * 1e3), transceiver_tolerance="-2 V ... +7 V common mode (SN65HVD230)", margin_x=round(2.0 / (v_motor + v_board))) print(json.dumps(out, indent=1)) json.dump(out, open("can_ground_report.json", "w"), indent=1)

A bus-off costs ~1.4 ms + one cycle: below the 20 ms CAN timeout, so the robot keeps balancing." }, "ground": { "motor_return_mOhm": 0.82, "perfboard_gnd_mOhm": 4.6, "worst_offset_mV": 60, "transceiver_tolerance": "-2 V ... +7 V common mode (SN65HVD230)", "margin_x": 33 } }

"""Electrical rules check of the robot wiring. Run: python3 erc.py -> erc_report.json + erc_report.md + robot.net Model: netlist.py (every harness wire from case/wiring.py + board internals). Checks: 1 shorts between supplies / supply and ground 6 firmware + Pi pin maps vs the wiring 2 one common ground 7 CAN bus: pair, nodes, termination 3 every power input supplied, in its voltage range 8 current per wire and per connector contact, rail budgets 4 logic nets: a driver, no two drivers, no input over its maximum, high level above the input threshold 5 dividers solved (sonar echo, sense inputs) 9 fuses vs the wires they protect """ import json, re, os, sys, collections sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) import netlist as N LEVEL = {'3V3': 3.3, '5V': 5.0} FINDINGS = [] UNRATED = [] def F(sev, check, msg, fix=''): FINDINGS.append(dict(sev=sev, check=check, msg=msg, fix=fix)) class UF: def __init__(s): s.p = {} def f(s, x): s.p.setdefault(x, x) while s.p[x] != x: s.p[x] = s.p[s.p[x]]; x = s.p[x] return x def u(s, a, b): s.p[s.f(a)] = s.f(b) def node(m, p): return f"{m}::{p}" def build(wires, key_in=True, fixed_key=False, button=False): """Return (uf, edges) where edges are (a, b, kind, ref) for path finding.""" uf, edges = UF(), [] for n in N.PINS: uf.f(n) for a, b, why in N.LINKS: uf.u(a, b); edges.append((a, b, 'link', why)) for i, w in enumerate(wires): a, b = node(*w['a']), node(*w['b']) uf.u(a, b); edges.append((a, b, 'wire', i)) if key_in: a, b, why = N.KEY_BRIDGE if fixed_key: a, b = node(N.KEY, 'contact A'), node(N.KEY, 'contact B') uf.u(a, b); edges.append((a, b, 'key', why)) if button: uf.u(node(N.BTN, 'BTN.closed'), node(N.BTN, 'Button + LED common')) return uf, edges def nets_of(uf): nets = collections.defaultdict(list) for n in list(uf.p): nets[uf.f(n)].append(n) return nets def attrs(n): return N.PINS.get(n, {}) def fix_key(wires): """The XT60 loop-key wiring as it must be: contact A = BAT+ from the fuse, contact B = BAT+ to the PDB, the two negatives spliced next to the socket (the key only interrupts the positive).""" out = [] for w in wires: w = dict(w); a, b = list(w['a']), list(w['b']) if b == [N.KEY, 'panel +'] and w['harness'].startswith('BMS'): b = [N.KEY, 'contact A'] if a == [N.KEY, 'panel +'] and w['harness'].startswith('XT60'): a = [N.KEY, 'contact B'] if b == [N.KEY, 'panel -']: b = [N.KEY, 'P- splice'] if a == [N.KEY, 'panel -']: a = [N.KEY, 'P- splice'] w['a'], w['b'] = a, b; out.append(w) for n in ('contact A', 'contact B', 'P- splice'): N.PINS.setdefault(node(N.KEY, n), dict(kind='pass')) return out # ---------------------------------------------------------------- checks def check_supplies(uf, tag): nets = nets_of(uf) bad = [] for r, ns in nets.items(): srcs = [n for n in ns if attrs(n).get('kind') == 'src'] gnds = [n for n in ns if attrs(n).get('kind') == 'gnd'] if srcs and gnds: bad.append((ns, f"supply {', '.join(srcs)} is tied to ground {', '.join(gnds[:3])}")) vs = {round(attrs(n)['V'], 1) for n in srcs if not attrs(n).get('charger')} if len(vs) > 1: bad.append((ns, f"supplies at different voltages on one net: {srcs}")) return bad def ground_net(uf): return uf.f(node(N.BAT, 'lead -')) def net_voltage(uf, root, nets): """DC voltage of a net: a supply on it, or through a diode from a supplied net.""" for n in nets[root]: a = attrs(n) if a.get('kind') == 'src': return a['V'] if a.get('kind') == 'gnd': return 0.0 for an, ca, vf, _ in N.DIODES: if uf.f(ca) == root: ra = uf.f(an) if ra != root: for n in nets[ra]: if attrs(n).get('kind') == 'src': return attrs(n)['V'] - vf return None def module(n): return n.split('::')[0] def solve_levels(uf, nets): """Logic/DC level of every net: drivers fix a net; resistor-only nets are solved by nodal analysis.""" fixed = {} for r, ns in nets.items(): v = net_voltage(uf, r, nets) if v is not None: fixed[r] = v; continue outs = [LEVEL[attrs(n)['level']] for n in ns if attrs(n).get('kind') == 'out' and attrs(n).get('level')] outs += [LEVEL[attrs(n)['level']] for n in ns if attrs(n).get('role') == 'out'] if outs: fixed[r] = max(outs) # resistor network unk = sorted({uf.f(x) for a, b, _, _ in N.RES for x in (a, b)} - set(fixed)) idx = {u: i for i, u in enumerate(unk)} import numpy as np G = np.zeros((len(unk), len(unk))); I = np.zeros(len(unk)) for a, b, ohm, _ in N.RES: ra, rb, g = uf.f(a), uf.f(b), 1.0 / ohm for x, y in ((ra, rb), (rb, ra)): if x in idx: G[idx[x], idx[x]] += g if y in idx: G[idx[x], idx[y]] -= g else: I[idx[x]] += g * fixed[y] levels = dict(fixed) floating = set() for u in unk: if G[idx[u], idx[u]] == 0: floating.add(u) if unk: keep = [u for u in unk if u not in floating] k = [idx[u] for u in keep] if k: v = np.linalg.lstsq(G[np.ix_(k, k)], I[k], rcond=None)[0] for u, x in zip(keep, v): levels[u] = float(x) return levels def has_res_path_to_fixed(uf, root, levels): return any(uf.f(a) == root or uf.f(b) == root for a, b, _, _ in N.RES) def check_power_inputs(uf, nets, levels): g = ground_net(uf) rows = [] for n, a in N.PINS.items(): if a.get('kind') != 'pin': continue r = uf.f(n); v = net_voltage(uf, r, nets) mod = module(n) gnd_ok = any(uf.f(p) == g for p, aa in N.PINS.items() if aa.get('kind') == 'gnd' and module(p) == mod) lo, hi = a['range'] rows.append((n, v, a['range'], gnd_ok)) if v is None: 'power inputs', f"{mod}: no ground pin on the common ground.") return rows def check_logic(uf, nets, levels): rows = [] for r, ns in nets.items(): ins = [n for n in ns if attrs(n).get('kind') in ('in', 'io') and attrs(n).get('role') not in ('out',)] if not ins: continue drivers = [n for n in ns if attrs(n).get('kind') == 'out' or attrs(n).get('role') == 'out' or attrs(n).get('kind') in attrs(n).get('role') == 'out'] v = levels.get(r) if len(pushpull) > 1: F('ERROR', 'logic', f"two outputs drive the same net: {pushpull}") if not drivers and not pulls and not has_res_path_to_fixed(uf, r, levels): sev = 'ERROR' if any(attrs(n).get('role') in ('in', 'adc') for n in ins) else 'WARN' F(sev, 'logic', f"input with nothing driving it: {', '.join(ins)}") for n in ins: a = attrs(n) if v is not None and a.get('vmax') is not None and v > a['vmax'] + 1e-6: F('ERROR', 'levels', f"{n} sees {v:.2f} V, its maximum is {a['vmax']} V.") th = a.get('vih') or (a.get('vih_frac') * 5.0 if drivers=drivers, v=None if v is None else round(v, 2))) return rows def device_ends(uf, nets, n, through_res=True): """Pins of other modules reachable from n (same net, or one resistor away).""" roots = {uf.f(n)} if through_res: for a, b, _, _ in N.RES: if uf.f(a) in roots: roots.add(uf.f(b)) elif uf.f(b) in roots: roots.add(uf.f(a)) return {p for r in roots for p in nets[r] if module(p) != """Mutation tests: each deliberate wiring mistake must be reported as an ERROR by erc.py.""" import copy, importlib, json, sys import netlist as N, erc as E BASE = N.wires() def run(mut): importlib.reload(N); importlib.reload(E) W = copy.deepcopy(BASE); mut(W) N.wires = lambda: W import io, contextlib with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()): E.main() return [f for f in E.FINDINGS if f['sev'] == 'ERROR'] def find(W, sig, harness=None): return next(w for w in W if w['sig'] == sig and (harness is None or w['harness'].startswith(harness))) def swap_uart(W): a, b = find(W, 'ESP TX (GPIO17) -> Pi RXD'), find(W, 'Pi TXD -> ESP RX (GPIO18)') a['b'], b['b'] = b['b'], a['b'] def old_key(W): """BMS P- landed on the power switch's VOUT instead of the negative splice: switching on shorts the battery.""" find(W, 'P-')['b'] = [N.KEY, 'VOUT (BAT+ to the PDB)'] def no_divider(W): find(W, 'ECHO (GPIO11 via 1k/2k)')['a'] = [N.PB, 'ESP.GPIO11'] def lose_ground(W): W.remove(find(W, 'GND', 'Perfboard J3')) def can_swap(W): h = find(W, 'CAN-H', 'CAN bus -> motor L'); l = find(W, 'CAN-L', 'CAN bus -> motor L') h['b'], l['b'] = l['b'], h['b'] def mic_5v(W): find(W, '3V', 'I2S junction -> mic L')['a'] = [N.JUN, '5 V'] def eye_from_pi_direct(W): find(W, 'DIN (via 330 ohm)')['a'] = [N.PB, 'J3-4 (ESP32 GPIO8)'] def no_sense(W): W.remove(find(W, 'VBAT sense (switched BAT+)')) CASES = [('UART TX/RX swapped', swap_uart), ('power switch: P- on VOUT', old_key), ('sonar echo without divider', no_divider), ('IMU ground missing', lose_ground), ('CAN H/L swapped at motor L', can_swap), ('mic on 5 V', mic_5v), ('eye data from a 3.3 V I2C pin', eye_from_pi_direct), ('VBAT sense wire missing', no_sense)] ok = True base = run(lambda W: None) print(f"baseline: {len(base)} errors") for name, m in CASES: errs = run(m) hit = bool(errs) ok &= hit print(f"{'caught' if hit else 'MISSED':7s} {name}: " + (errs[0]['msg'][:110] if errs else '')) sys.exit(0 if ok and not base else 1)

"""Linear static FEA (CalculiX) of the lower body under motor loads. Usage: python3 fea.py old|new Geometry: body_case.build_body() cut to the lower part (z -36..36), tet10 mesh (gmsh). Loads per motor, through the 4 M2.5 screws (hole wall + area under the head): - reaction torque T about the axle (both motors same direction: worst for the body) - wheel force Fz (ground pushing up, bumps/landing), moved from the wheel centre to the wall -> force + bending moment about x Fixed: the 4 floor insert bosses of the front panel / back cover screws (the only link to the shell). """ import sys, os, subprocess, json, numpy as np HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HERE, "..", "cad_scripts")) import cadquery as cq, body_case as bc, gmsh VAR = sys.argv[1] T_NMM = float(os.environ.get("T", 2300.0)) # 2.3 N.m: 16.5 A x 0.14 N.m/A, motor peak FZ = float(os.environ.get("FZ", 25.0)) # N per wheel: ~3 g on half the robot's weight E, NU = 2000.0, 0.38 # PETG, MPa H = float(os.environ.get("H", 1.4)) # mesh size at the motor walls (mm) WITH_SHELF = VAR == "reinf" and os.environ.get("NOSHELF", "0") != "1" SHELF = os.environ.get("SHELF", "0") == "1" # 1: the battery shelf holds the rail tops (y, z) OUT = os.path.join(HERE, "out", VAR) + ("_noshelf" if VAR == "reinf" and not WITH_SHELF else "") + ("_shelf" if SHELF else "") + os.environ.get("TAG", ""); os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True) # the two tray bosses touch the motor walls tangentially (r 4 at y 13 vs wall at 17): a zero-width sliver # that no mesher handles; merge them 1 mm into the wall for the analysis (no effect away from the floor) bc.FLOOR_TRAY_PTS = [(-24.0, -12.0), (21.0, 12.0)] if VAR == "old": bc.SLOT_W, bc.SLOT_Z = 19.0, (13.0, bc.SHELF_Z + 0.1) body = bc.build_body().val() ZC = 36.0 # the floor + motor-walls block is a separate solid from the shell (the wheel wells cut the floor off) lower = [s for s in body.Solids() if s.BoundingBox().zmin < -30][0] if WITH_SHELF: # shelf screwed to the wall tops: modelled as bonded lower = lower.fuse(bc.build_shelf().val()).clean() cq.exporters.export(cq.Workplane().add(lower), f"{OUT}/lower.step") # ---------------- mesh ---------------- gmsh.initialize(); gmsh.option.setNumber("General.Terminal", 0) for k_, v_ in [("Geometry.OCCFixDegenerated", 1), ("Geometry.OCCFixSmallEdges", 1), ("Geometry.OCCFixSmallFaces", 1), ("Geometry.OCCSewFaces", 1)]: gmsh.option.setNumber(k_, v_) gmsh.model.occ.importShapes(f"{OUT}/lower.step"); gmsh.model.occ.healShapes(); gmsh.model.occ.removeAllDuplicates(); gmsh.model.occ.synchronize() f = gmsh.model.mesh.field b1 = f.add("Box"); f.setNumber(b1, "VIn", H); f.setNumber(b1, "VOut", 3.2) f.setNumber(b1, "XMin", -32); f.setNumber(b1, "XMax", 29); f.setNumber(b1, "YMin", -26); f.setNumber(b1, "YMax", 26) f.setNumber(b1, "ZMin", -36); f.setNumber(b1, "ZMax", 37); f.setNumber(b1, "Thickness", 8) f.setAsBackgroundMesh(b1) gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.MeshSizeExtendFromBoundary", 0); gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.MeshSizeFromPoints", 0) gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.MeshSizeFromCurvature", 0) gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.ElementOrder", 2); gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.HighOrderOptimize", 0); gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.SecondOrderLinear", 1) gmsh.option.setNumber("Mesh.Algorithm3D", int(os.environ.get("ALG3", 1))) gmsh.model.mesh.generate(3) tag, xyz, _ = gmsh.model.mesh.getNodes() X = xyz.reshape(-1, 3); idx = {int(t): i for i, t in enumerate(tag)} et, etags, enodes = gmsh.model.mesh.getElements(3) k = list(et).index(11) # 10-node tet tets = np.array([idx[int(n)] for n in enodes[k]]).reshape(-1, 10) gmsh.finalize() print(f"{VAR}: {len(X)} nodes, {len(tets)} tet10") # ---------------- BCs and loads ---------------- # supports: the 4 floor bosses where the front panel and back cover screw on (M3 inserts, y +-40, z -28.5). # The panels tie this block to the upper shell; they are treated as rigid. zb = bc.Z_FLOOR + 3.5 ri = bc.INSERT_D / 2 fixed = np.where((np.abs(np.hypot(np.abs(X[:, 1]) - 40.0, X[:, 2] - zb) - ri) < 0.08) & ((X[:, 0] > bc.X_IN_F - bc.INS_M3[1] - 0.1) | (X[:, 0] < bc.X_BACK + bc.INS_M3[1] + 0.1)))[0] rails = np.where(X[:, 2] > bc.SHELF_Z + bc.RAIL_H - 0.05)[0] if SHELF else np.array([], int) print("fixed nodes", len(fixed), "rail nodes", len(rails)) F = np.zeros_like(X) HOLES = [(-10, -10), (10, -10), (10, 10), (-10, 10)] rh = bc.M25_CLEAR / 2 for s in (1, -1): yin = s * bc.GAP_HALF # inner wall face (screw heads) ywall = s * (bc.GAP_HALF + bc.MWALL_T / 2) yw = s * (bc.WHEEL_IN_Y + bc.WHEEL_W / 2) d = yw - ywall for (xc, zc) in HOLES: rr = np.hypot(X[:, 0] - xc, X[:, 2] - zc) inwall = (s * X[:, 1] > bc.GAP_HALF - 0.05) & (s * X[:, 1] < bc.GAP_HALF + bc.MWALL_T + 0.05) shank = inwall & (np.abs(rr - rh) < 0.08) head = (np.abs(X[:, 1] - yin) < 0.05) & (rr > rh - 0.05) & (rr < 2.4) sel = np.where(shank | head)[0] fh = np.array([T_NMM / (4 * 200.0) * zc, 0.0, -T_NMM / (4 * 200.0) * xc]) # sum r x F = T about y fh += np.array([0.0, -d * FZ * zc / 400.0, FZ / 4]) # Fz + moment d*Fz about x F[sel] += fh / len(sel) assert abs(F[:, 2].sum() - 2 * FZ) < 1e-6 # ---------------- CalculiX ---------------- with open(f"{OUT}/job.inp", "w") as o: o.write("*NODE, NSET=NALL\n") for i, p in enumerate(X): o.write(f"{i+1},{p[0]:.6f},{p[1]:.6f},{p[2]:.6f}\n") o.write("*ELEMENT, TYPE=C3D10, ELSET=EALL\n") perm = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 8] # gmsh -> abaqus/ccx edge-node order for j, t in enumerate(tets): o.write(f"{j+1}," + ",".join(str(t[p] + 1) for p in perm) + "\n") o.write("*NSET, NSET=FIX\n" + "\n".join(str(i + 1) for i in fixed) + "\n") o.write(f"*MATERIAL, NAME=PETG\n*ELASTIC\n{E},{NU}\n*SOLID SECTION, ELSET=EALL, MATERIAL=PETG\n") if len(rails): o.write("*NSET, NSET=RAIL\n" + "\n".join(str(i + 1) for i in rails) + "\n") o.write("*STEP\n*STATIC\n*BOUNDARY\nFIX,1,3,0\n" + ("RAIL,2,3,0\n" if len(rails) else "") + "*CLOAD\n") for i in np.where(np.abs(F).sum(1) > 0)[0]: for c in range(3): if F[i, c] != 0: o.write(f"{i+1},{c+1},{F[i, c]:.6e}\n") o.write("*NODE FILE\nU\n*EL FILE\nS\n*END STEP\n") subprocess.run(["ccx", "-i", "job"], cwd=OUT, check=True, stdout=open(f"{OUT}/ccx.log", "w")) # ---------------- read results ---------------- def read_frd(path, name, ncomp): out = {}; on = False for line in open(path): if line.startswith(" -4") and name in line: on = True; continue if on: if line.startswith(" -3"): break if line.startswith(" -1"): n = int(line[3:13]); out[n] = [float(line[13 + 12 * c:25 + 12 * c]) for c in range(ncomp)] a = np.zeros((len(X), ncomp)) for n, v in out.items(): a[n - 1] = v return a U = read_frd(f"{OUT}/job.frd", "DISP", 3) S = read_frd(f"{OUT}/job.frd", "STRESS", 6) # xx yy zz xy yz zx sx, sy, sz, txy, tyz, tzx = S.T vm = np.sqrt(0.5 * ((sx - sy) ** 2 + (sy - sz) ** 2 + (sz - sx) ** 2) + 3 * (txy ** 2 + tyz ** 2 + tzx ** 2)) np.savez_compressed(f"{OUT}/res.npz", X=X, tets=tets[:, :4], U=U, S=S, vm=vm, F=F) # exclude the load-introduction points (local bearing under the screws, real but not a structural weakness) near = np.zeros(len(X), bool) for (xc, zc) in HOLES: near |= (np.hypot(X[:, 0] - xc, X[:, 2] - zc) < 3.2) & (np.abs(X[:, 1]) < 25) def region(m): i = np.where(m & ~near)[0]; j = i[np.argmax(vm[i])] return dict(vm=round(float(vm[j]), 2), sx_tension=round(float(sx[i].max()), 2), at=[round(float(v), 1) for v in X[j]]) wall = (np.abs(X[:, 1]) > 16.9) & (np.abs(X[:, 1]) < 24.1) res = { "variant": VAR, "nodes": len(X), "T_Nm": T_NMM / 1000, "Fz_N": FZ, "max_disp_mm": round(float(np.linalg.norm(U, axis=1).max()), 4), "motor_wall_twist_deg": None, "everywhere": region(np.ones(len(X), bool)), "motor_walls": region(wall), "wall_above_axle_z12_36": region(wall & (X[:, 2] > 12)), "wall_floor_junction": region(wall & (X[:, 2] < -27)), "floor_bosses": region((np.abs(np.abs(X[:, 1]) - 40) < 8) & (X[:, 2] < -20)), "rest_of_body": region(~wall & (X[:, 2] < bc.SHELF_Z - 0.05)), "shelf": region(X[:, 2] > bc.SHELF_Z + 0.05) if (X[:, 2] > bc.SHELF_Z + 0.05).any() else None, "screw_bearing_max": round(float(vm[near].max()), 2), } # rotation of the motor mount (rigid-body fit of the hole-node displacements) -> how much the motor axis tilts for s in (1, -1): m = (s * X[:, 1] > bc.GAP_HALF - 0.05) & (s * X[:, 1] < bc.GAP_HALF + bc.MWALL_T + 0.05) & near P = X[m] - X[m].mean(0); D = U[m] - U[m].mean(0) A = np.zeros((3 * len(P), 3)); b = D.reshape(-1) for q, p in enumerate(P): # D = w x p A[3 * q] = [0, p[2], -p[1]]; A[3 * q + 1] = [-p[2], 0, p[0]]; A[3 * q + 2] = [p[1], -p[0], 0] w = np.linalg.lstsq(A, b, rcond=None)[0] res[f"mount_rotation_deg_side{s:+d}"] = [round(float(np.degrees(v)), 4) for v in w] res[f"mount_shift_mm_side{s:+d}"] = [round(float(v), 4) for v in U[m].mean(0)] del res["motor_wall_twist_deg"] json.dump(res, open(f"{OUT}/summary.json", "w"), indent=1) print(json.dumps(res, indent=1))

import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use("Agg") import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from render import surface, draw def load(d): r = np.load(f"out/{d}/res.npz"); return r["X"], surface(r["tets"]), r["vm"] VMAX = 20.0 cases = [("new", "Before: shelf only sliding on rails (loose)\nmax 20.5 MPa · motor axis tilts 3.3°"), ("reinf", "Now: shelf screwed, fillets, ribs, deeper body\nmax 5.4 MPa · motor axis tilts 0.24°")] fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7.4, 9.0), dpi=130) for i, (d, t) in enumerate(cases): X, F, vm = load(d) ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 2 * i + 1, projection="3d"); draw(ax, X, F, vm, 28, -128, VMAX, title=t) ax = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 2 * i + 2, projection="3d"); draw(ax, X, F, vm, -32, 58, VMAX, title="from below") sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(cmap="turbo", norm=plt.Normalize(0, VMAX)) cb = fig.colorbar(sm, ax=fig.axes, orientation="horizontal", fraction=0.03, pad=0.03) cb.set_label("von Mises (MPa) · peak torque 2.3 N·m + 25 N per wheel · PETG layer bond ≈ 20–30 MPa") plt.savefig("fea_before_after.png", bbox_inches="tight"); print("ok")

"""Render von Mises stress on the outer surface of a CalculiX result (res.npz).""" import sys, numpy as np, matplotlib matplotlib.use("Agg") import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d.art3d import Poly3DCollection def surface(tets): f = np.concatenate([tets[:, [0, 2, 1]], tets[:, [0, 1, 3]], tets[:, [1, 2, 3]], tets[:, [0, 3, 2]]]) k = np.sort(f, 1); _, idx, cnt = np.unique(k, axis=0, return_index=True, return_counts=True) return f[idx[cnt == 1]] def draw(ax, X, F, vm, elev, azim, vmax, lim=None, title=""): if lim is not None: c = X[F].mean(1); m = np.all((c >= lim[0]) & (c <= lim[1]), 1); F = F[m] tri = X[F]; val = vm[F].mean(1) n = np.cross(tri[:, 1] - tri[:, 0], tri[:, 2] - tri[:, 0]); n /= np.linalg.norm(n, axis=1)[:, None] + 1e-12 e, a = np.radians(elev), np.radians(azim) view = np.array([np.cos(e) * np.cos(a), np.cos(e) * np.sin(a), np.sin(e)]) shade = 0.55 + 0.45 * np.abs(n @ view) col = plt.cm.turbo(np.clip(val / vmax, 0, 1)); col[:, :3] *= shade[:, None] depth = tri.mean(1) @ view; o = np.argsort(depth) ax.add_collection3d(Poly3DCollection(tri[o], facecolors=col[o], edgecolors="none", linewidths=0)) lo, hi = (X.min(0), X.max(0)) if lim is None else (np.array(lim[0]), np.array(lim[1])) ax.set_xlim(lo[0], hi[0]); ax.set_ylim(lo[1], hi[1]); ax.set_zlim(lo[2], hi[2]) ax.set_box_aspect(hi - lo); ax.view_init(elev, azim); ax.set_axis_off(); ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10) if __name__ == "__main__": pass

"""Virtual LK MF6015 motors on the MuJoCo robot, shared by the QEMU test (hil/run_hil.py) and the real-CAN bench (bench/bench_hil.py). LK CAN protocol V2: 0x88 on / 0x80 off (reply = echo of the command), 0x9C read state 2 and 0x280 multi-motor torque (replies [cmd, temp, iq, speed dps, encoder] from 0x141/0x142).""" import math, os, struct, sys, pathlib import numpy as np, mujoco ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "sim")) from botsim import BotSim, CTRL_DT, KT, I_MAX, quat_pitch # noqa: E402,F401 (plant, motor model, IMU model) ENC_BITS = int(os.environ.get("ENC_BITS", "16")) ENC_RANGE = 1 << ENC_BITS ID_L, ID_R, ID_MULTI = 0x141, 0x142, 0x280 DIR = {ID_L: +1, ID_R: -1} # must match config.h DIR_LEFT/DIR_RIGHT IQ_FULL, IQ_MAX = 16.5, 2048 def crc(p): c = 0 for b in p: c = (((c << 1) | (c >> 7)) & 0xFF) ^ b return c def frame(t, payload): body = bytes([t, len(payload)]) + payload return b"\xA5\x5A" + body + bytes([crc(body)]) class Plant(BotSim): """MuJoCo robot driven by external motor commands (the firmware), with the LK drive model of botsim.""" def __init__(self, seed, randomize=True): super().__init__(seed=seed, randomize=randomize) self.on = {ID_L: False, ID_R: False} self.iq_cmd = {ID_L: 0, ID_R: 0} self.t_fw = None; self.rem = 0.0 self.push = None; self.push_until = 0.0 self.hold = None self.trace = [] def joint_w(self, side): return self.d.qvel[self.m.jnt_dofadr[self.m.joint(f"{side}_hinge").id]] def advance(self, dt): n = int((dt + self.rem) / self.m.opt.timestep + 1e-9) self.rem = dt + self.rem - n * self.m.opt.timestep for _ in range(n): tq = [] for mid, side in ((ID_L, "left"), (ID_R, "right")): tau = DIR[mid] * self.iq_cmd[mid] * IQ_FULL / IQ_MAX * KT if self.on[mid] else 0.0 tq.append(self.motor(tau, self.joint_w(side))) self.d.ctrl[:] = tq if self.push is not None and self.t < self.push_until: self.d.xfrc_applied[self.ch, :3] = self.push else: self.d.xfrc_applied[self.ch, :3] = 0 mujoco.mj_step(self.m, self.d) if self.hold is not None: self.d.qpos[:] = self.hold; self.d.qvel[:] = 0; mujoco.mj_forward(self.m, self.d) self.t += self.m.opt.timestep self.trace.append((self.t, quat_pitch(self.d.qpos[3:7]), float(self.d.qpos[0]), float(self.d.qpos[1]), self.on[ID_L], self.iq_cmd[ID_L], self.iq_cmd[ID_R])) def imu(self): s = self.sense() return struct.pack("<6f", s.ax, s.ay, s.az, s.gx, s.gy, s.gz) def reply(self, mid, cmd): """LK V2 reply: [cmd, temp, iq, speed dps, encoder] (0xA1 / 0x9C).""" s, sd = self.d.sensordata, self.sid q = s[sd["ql"]] if mid == ID_L else s[sd["qr"]] # wheel angle relative to the body, robot-forward + w = s[sd["wl"]] if mid == ID_L else s[sd["wr"]] raw = DIR[mid] * q enc = int(round((raw / (2 * math.pi)) * ENC_RANGE)) % ENC_RANGE dps = int(round(math.degrees(DIR[mid] * w))) iq = int(self.iq_cmd[mid] if self.on[mid] else 0) return struct.pack("<BbhhH", cmd, 30, iq, max(-32768, min(32767, dps)), enc) class VirtualLK: """Answers LK frames for motors 1 (0x141) and 2 (0x142) from the plant's state. handle() returns the reply frames.""" def __init__(self, plant): self.p = plant self.mute_until = -1.0 # plant time until which the motors are silent (CAN unplugged) self.rx = 0; self.tx = 0 def handle(self, cid, d): P = self.p; d = bytes(d) self.rx += 1 if P.t < self.mute_until or len(d) < 8: return [] cmd = d[0]; out = [] if cid == ID_MULTI: a, b = struct.unpack("<hh", d[:4]) P.iq_cmd[ID_L], P.iq_cmd[ID_R] = max(-IQ_MAX, min(IQ_MAX, a)), max(-IQ_MAX, min(IQ_MAX, b)) out = [(mid, P.reply(mid, 0xA1)) for mid in (ID_L, ID_R)] elif cid in (ID_L, ID_R): if cmd == 0x88: P.on[cid] = True if cmd == 0x80: P.on[cid] = False; P.iq_cmd[cid] = 0 if cmd in (0x80, 0x88): out = [(cid, d)] # LK manual: reply = the command itself elif cmd == 0x9C: out = [(cid, P.reply(cid, 0x9C))] elif cmd == 0xA1: # single-motor torque (probe tool) P.iq_cmd[cid] = max(-IQ_MAX, min(IQ_MAX, struct.unpack("<h", d[4:6])[0])); P.on[cid] = True out = [(cid, P.reply(cid, 0xA1))] self.tx += len(out) return out
